topic: Breath series 4: Cyclic sighing (animated, guided, research)
caption:
Cyclic sighing slows down a sigh your body already does, and repeats it.

In a lab study, tension tended to build before a natural sigh and ease after it, but one sigh on cue after a stressful task didn't ease it the same way. In a month-long Stanford study, five minutes of daily cyclic sighing lifted mood more than mindfulness meditation. Both studies were small, mostly with young, healthy adults.

How to try it: take a full, slow inhale through your nose. At the top, take one short, sharp sniff in to fully expand your lungs. Then breathe out in one long, slow exhale through your mouth. The Reel paces it at about three seconds in, one for the sniff and eight out, but go at your own pace.

If you feel light-headed, go back to your usual breathing. Research on this technique has excluded people with heart disease, glaucoma, a history of seizures or pregnancy, so check with your doctor first if any of these apply to you.

Save this for another time.
